:::{#def-sum-over-set}
#### Sum over a finite set

Let $A = \cb{x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k}$ be a finite [set](sets-functions.qmd#def-set)
with $k \ge 1$ different elements.
Let $f$ be a [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function)
that gives a number $f(x)$ for each element $x$ of $A$.
The **sum of $f$ over $A$** is

$$
\sum_{x \in A} f(x) \eqdef f(x_1) + f(x_2) + \cdots + f(x_k)
$$

If $A$ has no elements, the sum has no terms,
and by convention it equals $0$.
For example, $\sum_{x \in \cb{}} x^2 = 0$.

:::

::: notes
The order in which we list the elements of $A$ does not change the sum.
The reason is that addition is commutative and associative:
we can reorder and regroup the terms of a finite sum
without changing the total.
@exr-sum-over-set, part 2, shows one example.
When $A = \cb{m, m+1, \ldots, n}$,
this sum is the same as $\sum_{i=m}^{n} f(i)$ from @def-summation.

Some authors leave the set out and write $\sum_{x} f(x)$.
This shorthand means the sum over every value $x$ can take.
For example, if $x$ is the outcome of one roll of a six-sided die,
$\sum_{x} f(x)$ means $\sum_{x \in \cb{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}} f(x)$.
In these notes, we write the set out in full.
:::
